games.science.magnetLab.title: Magnet Lab
games.science.magnetLab.howTo: Sort things by what a magnet does. Then tell if two magnets pull together or push apart.
games.science.magnetLab.sortQuestion: Which things does a magnet pull? Sort them.
games.science.magnetLab.rule.sticks: A magnet pulls things made of iron or steel.
games.science.magnetLab.rule.notSticks: A magnet does not pull wood, plastic, glass, paper, or metals like aluminium and copper.
games.science.magnetLab.polesQuestion: The two magnets face each other. Will they pull together or push apart?
games.science.magnetLab.polesLabel: Two bar magnets face to face. The ends that meet are {{a}} and {{b}}.
games.science.magnetLab.explainRepel: The same poles push apart: N and N, or S and S.
games.science.magnetLab.explainAttract: Different poles pull together: N and S.
games.science.magnetLab.pickupQuestion: Which one will the magnet pick up?
games.science.magnetLab.explainPickup: {{item}} is made of iron or steel, so the magnet picks it up.
games.science.lightShadows.title: Light and Shadows
games.science.lightShadows.howTo: Sort things by light: what makes light, and what lets light through, blocks it, or lets a little through.
games.science.lightShadows.sourceQuestio: Which things make their own light? Sort them.
games.science.lightShadows.materialQuest: What does each thing do to light? Sort them.
games.science.lightShadows.rule.notSourc: It makes no light of its own; we see it when other light bounces off it.
games.science.lightShadows.rule.opaque: Opaque things block light, so they make a dark shadow.
games.science.lightShadows.rule.transpar: Transparent things let light pass through, so we can see clearly through them.
games.science.lightShadows.rule.transluc: Translucent things let some light through, so we cannot see clearly through them.
games.science.soundDetective.title: Sound Detective
games.science.soundDetective.howTo: Tell loud sounds from soft ones, high from low, and find out how sound travels.
games.science.soundDetective.loudOrSoft: Is the sound of {{item}} loud or soft?
games.science.soundDetective.highOrLow: Is the sound of {{item}} high or low?
games.science.soundDetective.ask.high: Which sound is the highest, like a thin squeak?
games.science.soundDetective.ask.low: Which sound is the lowest, like a deep rumble?
games.science.soundDetective.explain.lou: {{item}} makes a big, strong sound, so it is loud.
games.science.soundDetective.explain.sof: {{item}} makes a small, gentle sound, so it is soft.
games.science.soundDetective.explain.hig: {{item}} makes a thin, squeaky sound, so it is high.
games.science.soundDetective.explain.low: {{item}} makes a deep, rumbling sound, so it is low.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.v: Sound is made when something vibrates (shakes quickly).
When a drum skin shakes, you hear a sound.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.w: Water carries sound, so divers can hear a boat engine.
Sound can travel through a wooden door.
Sound goes through solids like wood, so we hear knocks from the other side.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.a: Sound travels through air to reach our ears.
Air carries the sound from the thing to our ears.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.s: Sound can travel through empty space where there is no air.
Sound needs air, water or a solid to travel through, and empty space has none of them.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.e: We hear sounds with our ears.
Our ears catch sounds and tell the brain.
We hear sounds with our eyes.
We hear with our ears, and we see with our eyes.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.s: A drum makes a sound even when its skin is perfectly still.
A drum only makes a sound when its skin shakes.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.h: Hitting a drum harder makes a louder sound.
A harder hit shakes the drum skin more, so the sound is louder.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.s: A short, thin string makes a higher sound than a long, thick one.
Short, thin strings shake faster, so their sound is higher.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.t: Nature makes thunder; nobody made it.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.b: A bird's song is an artificial sound.
A bird's song is a natural sound; artificial sounds come from things people made.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.h: A car horn is an artificial sound.
People made the horn, so its sound is artificial.
games.science.soundDetective.statement.m: Music and noise are the same thing.
Music is a pleasant mix of sounds, and noise is an unpleasant, jumbled sound.
games.science.waterCycleOrder.title: Water Cycle Order
games.science.waterCycleOrder.howTo: Put the steps of the water story in the right order, from first to last.
games.science.waterCycleOrder.question: What happens first, next and last? Put the steps in order.
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.seaW: The sun warms the sea water
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.vapo: Water turns into vapour and rises
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.clou: The vapour cools and makes clouds
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.back: The river carries the water back to the sea
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.sunS: The sun shines on the puddle
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.vapo: The vapour goes up into the air
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.stre: Water runs down in a stream
games.science.waterCycleOrder.stage.lake: The sun warms the lake water
games.science.foodChainBuilder.title: Food Chain Builder
games.science.foodChainBuilder.howTo: Build food chains: the plant comes first, then the animal that eats it. Later, sort living things by what they eat.
games.science.foodChainBuilder.chainQues: Build the food chain. Start with the plant, then who eats it, then who eats that.
games.science.foodChainBuilder.explainCh: A food chain starts with a plant, and each living thing is food for the next: {{order}}.
games.science.foodChainBuilder.sortQuest: What does each one eat? Sort them.
games.science.foodChainBuilder.rule.plan: Plants make their own food using sunlight.
games.science.circuitBuilder.title: Electric Circuit Builder
games.science.circuitBuilder.howTo: Fix small battery circuits. Find the missing part, tell if the bulb will light, then sort materials that carry electricity.
games.science.circuitBuilder.safety: Safety: only try this with a small battery. Never put anything into a wall socket.
games.science.circuitBuilder.missingQues: A part is missing from this circuit. Which part must go in the gap?
games.science.circuitBuilder.explainMiss: The battery pushes the electricity round the circuit, so the circuit needs it.
The bulb is the part that lights up, so it must be in the circuit.
The switch lets us close the circuit, so it must fill the gap.
games.science.circuitBuilder.labelMissin: A circuit loop with a battery, a switch and a bulb. One part is missing and shows as a dashed gap with a question mark.
games.science.circuitBuilder.labelSolved: The circuit is complete and the bulb is lit.
games.science.circuitBuilder.label.none: A complete circuit with a battery, a closed switch and a bulb.
games.science.circuitBuilder.label.switc: A circuit where the switch is open, so there is a gap.
games.science.circuitBuilder.label.wireB: A circuit where the wire at the bottom is broken.
games.science.circuitBuilder.label.noBat: A circuit with no battery: there is an empty gap.
games.science.circuitBuilder.label.noBul: A circuit with no bulb: there is an empty gap.
games.science.circuitBuilder.explainFaul: The circuit is a complete loop with a battery and a closed switch, so electricity flows and the bulb lights.
The switch is open, so the circuit has a gap and the bulb stays off.
The wire is broken, so the circuit has a gap and the bulb stays off.
There is no battery to push the electricity, so the bulb stays off.
There is no bulb in the circuit, so there is nothing to light up.
games.science.circuitBuilder.sortQuestio: Test each material in the circuit. Does it let electricity through? Sort them.
games.science.circuitBuilder.rule.conduc: Metals and graphite let electricity flow through them.
games.science.circuitBuilder.rule.insula: Plastic, rubber, wood, glass, paper and cloth do not let electricity flow.

games.sinhala.fixSpelling.explainOdd: That word has a mistake. It should be {{word}}, with the letter {{letter}}.
